802.1X blocks data on the wired port until EAPOL and RADIUS/UDP1812 authorize the MAC. TACACS+ uses TCP/49 for CHAP, command authorization and session accounting. Configure commands on the user; ["*"] permits all commands allowed by the privilege level. For PEAP/TLS enterprise Wi-Fi, use the EAP configuration in the enterprise features tab. The wired port uses CHAP challenge/response and octet-encoded RADIUS. Enterprise PEAP/TLS is in the EAP configuration; TACACS+ uses separate authorization and body obfuscation. A VLAN returned by RADIUS must exist on the switch. The enforceCli option requires privilege 15 for configuration from the terminal.
RADIUS server for EAP TLS/PEAP: authorize the AP with the shared key and configure users and the server identity. The example authority belongs to the lab.
The AP authenticates the client against a RADIUS server reachable over the IPv4 underlay. Use a WPA2-Enterprise SSID; the client must trust the server's authority.
The client uses a certificate with EAP-TLS or a password with PEAP. Configure the WPA2-Enterprise SSID and the trusted authority of the RADIUS server.
The controller manages APs via CAPWAP. Configure IPv4 on the underlay, WLAN profiles and the key shared with the APs. Transport uses UDP/5246 for control and /5247 for data.
This managed AP needs an IPv4 route to the controller and a matching WLAN profile and key. The controller delivers the configuration after CAPWAP discovery and join.
APs in the same mesh use a common identity, key and channel. Mark the AP with the wired uplink as root. Priority selects the root, and the metric determines the path between neighbors.
IDS monitors signatures and rates and raises alerts. IPS can drop traffic that matches the rules. In this model, inspection acts on the device's forwarding path.
For a load balancer, use kind: load-balancer, port: 80 and backends. For a proxy, allowedNetworks contains the allowed destination IPs.
Subscriptions use QoS 0. Authentication does not encrypt the transport; TLS, QoS 2 and persistent sessions are not yet available in this model.

BGP exchanges OPEN, KEEPALIVE and UPDATE over TCP/179. AS_PATH prevents loops; LOCAL_PREF and filters define the policy. NEXT_HOP needs a route in the underlay. Advance the events to negotiate and observe withdrawals. Applying resets the sessions.
The prefix must exist in the router's routing table as a connected, static or IGP route.
One per line: IP remote-AS. Options: passive, next-hop-self, rr-client, local-pref=N, med=N, prepend=N.
First matching rule by sequence wins. A configured filter has an implicit deny; without rules, valid prefixes are permitted.
> marks the installed path. iBGP uses distance 200; eBGP, 20. Route reflectors use ORIGINATOR_ID/CLUSTER_LIST to prevent loops.

Choose both ports and a physically compatible medium.
Serial requires DCE/DTE interfaces and up to 50 m. The DCE clock sets the transmission rate.
Console requires compatible UART ports, the same baud rate and up to 15 m.
DAC requires DAC modules, matching sockets and a distance of up to 7 m.
Fiber requires compatible transceivers at both ends. Catalog SFP ports come with single-mode modules.
RJ45 · up to 100 m in the model. Ports use conceptual Auto-MDIX, accepting straight-through or crossover cables.

Reads and writes respond only after majority confirmation. Use the leader's individual IP; new connections can use discovery with explicit replicas and cluster. There is no TCP migration or automatic VIP on this server.

History is compacted automatically, with up to 256 retained entries and 512 KiB of materialized data. A timeout has an indeterminate result; query the leader before retrying a write. Removing a member/group disables the databases while preserving local data.
Enable empty databases with the same port and key on all members. Wait for quorum synchronization before binding the group.
Lab service: CREATE TABLE, INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE. Maximum of 16 tables, 16 columns and 256 rows per table. Does not use the PostgreSQL protocol.

CREATE TABLE sensors (id, value) INSERT INTO sensors (id, value) VALUES (1, 23.5) SELECT * FROM sensors WHERE id = 1 LIMIT 10 UPDATE sensors SET value = 24 WHERE id = 1 DELETE FROM sensors WHERE id = 1
Each replica is queried over the network. The SQL query is sent once to the confirmed leader. If the response is lost, check the result before retrying a write.
